items: Osmoconformers let the osmotic concentration of their body fluids match the environment; they stay isotonic with it and cannot keep their own concentrations. They live where solute levels are fairly stable, such as the sea: all marine invertebrates, some freshwater invertebrates, and some marine vertebrates such as hagfishes, sharks and rays.

Osmoregulators keep the concentrations of water and solutes in their body fluids constant despite changes outside, using active transport of salts, accumulation of salts and water conservation. Most aquatic and terrestrial vertebrates are osmoregulators.

blocks.prompt: Define osmoregulators and osmoconformers, with one example of each.
blocks.explanation: Osmoconformers let their body fluids match the surroundings (a marine invertebrate such as a starfish, or a hagfish); osmoregulators keep their body fluids constant whatever the surroundings (a freshwater fish or a human).

items: Osmoconformers match the environment (marine invertebrates); osmoregulators control their own concentration (most vertebrates).
